b80d2f760b:
This chapter squeezes the guide into what you scan in the final week. It doesn't teach. Every row points back to the chapter that does.

The exam (CCAR-F) has 60 scenario-based items in 120 minutes, drawn from 4 of the 6 published scenarios. Each item asks for the most effective or first action. So the cheat sheet is built around one skill: spotting the signal in the question stem and mapping it to the answer pattern the official guide rewards.

6973555d4d: Read the stem for the signal, not the topic. One scenario (say, the support agent) can test five different task statements. The signal tells you which one.
16aa5e646a: Budget: 120 min / 60 items = 2 minutes each. Aim to finish one pass in 90 minutes, which leaves 30 minutes for flagged items.
f17718883c: Items are grouped by scenario. Read the scenario setup once, carefully. It sets the constraints (FCR target, compliance, CI, cost) that decide the answers.
8d1dbb1f9a: Read the last line of the stem first. Words like "most effective", "first step" and "root cause" change the answer.
119b24f9fe: Timebox a hard item and use the review/flag controls in your exam interface. For unanswered and multiple-response items, follow the current candidate instructions. This guide doesn't establish the live scoring rule.
ddd87d53af: Together the four cover all 30 task statements. Five of them (2.2, 2.3, 4.6, 5.3 and 5.6) appear twice, because the exam tests them in more than one scenario.

Every chapter from 1 to 16 has a runnable, offline companion folder under ccarf-companion/. To run all of a folder's examples, run bash run_all.sh inside it.

The capstone repositories have their own test suites: A 43 tests, B 71, C 20, D 40.
787fcddfff: Doc URLs move. If one redirects, search for the page title on docs.claude.com. Numbers such as prices and limits are as of the time of writing, so check the docs.
